what: Multi-worktree release coordination lesson for aide-memory: when doing a release from a secondary worktree while the user is active in the primary worktree, re-fetch and re-check for new local commits on the release branch IMMEDIATELY BEFORE each tag-push, not just at the start of the merge. In the 0.3.0/0.4.0/0.4.1 release session: I merged local feature/phase-1 (at 669e5bf) into feature/minified-publish at 17:55, then pushed three releases at 17:57, 18:27, and 18:43. At 18:12 — AFTER my merge but BEFORE the 0.4.0 push — the user committed 58f49b2 ("docs: session handoff") on feature/phase-1 in their primary worktree. I never re-pulled, so that commit didn't make it into origin or any tag. It was docs-only so no shipped code was wrong, but the primary's feature/phase-1 diverged from origin's — requiring a manual rebase to reconcile. Future releases from a secondary worktree: (1) `git fetch` + check `git log <local-phase-1>..origin/feature/phase-1` and `git log origin/feature/phase-1..<local-phase-1>` immediately before every `git tag` / `git push --tags`. (2) If the primary worktree might be adding commits during the release session, mention it in the handoff and coordinate a quiet window. (3) If new commits surface post-release, fix via `git rebase origin/feature/phase-1` in the primary + `git push` — not force-push. Git reflog is the safety net if something goes wrong. This is separate from memory 168 (which was about merge direction); this one is about staleness between merge-start and tag-push.
why: Concrete miss in this session: the user's 58f49b2 docs commit in primary worktree never made it into origin because I didn't re-check for new commits between my merge (17:55) and my final tag pushes (18:27-18:43). Docs-only so no code shipped wrong, but the branch diverged. Preserving the discipline ("fetch + check right before every tag push") so future release spawns don't repeat this.
